chunks: Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who hired a wet nurse and gave her his child, and the child remained with her. Then the wet nurse went and hired another wet nurse, and the wet nurse disappeared with the child, so it was not known what had been done with him, and the wet nurse could not be matched in retaliation. He عليه السلام said: The full blood money is due.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated it from Ibn Miskān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, similarly. And Ḥammād narrated it from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, similarly.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ كَامِلَةً: the full blood money is legally due
key_terms.بِالْوَلَدِ: with the child entrusted to her care
key_terms.ظِئْرًا: a wet nurse hired to suckle and care for an infant
key_terms.لَا تُكَافَى: she is not subject to equivalent retaliation in this case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wet nurse hands a child to another wet nurse who disappears with the child?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning liability when a hired wet nurse entrusts the child to another wet nurse who then disappears with the child. The ruling states that the full diyyah is due, establishing financial liability in a case where the child's fate becomes unknown through such transfer.
